Four services, each done the same careful way. Here's what to expect.

Installation

Round and oval pools.

A pool is only as good as the ground under it. We level the site, set the track, and build the wall square before a drop of water goes in.

  • Site prep and ground leveling
  • Bottom track, wall, uprights and top rails
  • Liner set, filled, and wrinkle-free
  • Pump and filter hookup
Round 15′–33′Oval 12×17′–18×40′48″–54″ walls

See installation prices

Installation

What to expect on install day.

Most installs take 4 to 8 hours, depending on pool size and how level your yard is.

Before we arrive

Please have these done before install day.

  • Get a permit from your city. What you'll need
  • Call MISS DIG (811) to have underground utilities marked.
  • Have clean washed masonry sand delivered. Sand reference table
  • Get two 2′×2′ patio blocks for the filter system to sit on.
  • Mark your pool spot. Round pool: put a stake where you want the center. Oval pool: mark the four corners of a rectangle. See the reference pictures below.
  • Mark your filter spot with another stake. Filters go 3′ off the water's edge. On an oval pool, the filter must go on one of the curved ends.
  • Customer to build ladder. Due to insurance liability, Brightside Pools is not allowed to build or install ladders. We recommend waiting 4 to 5 days after installation before setting your ladder, allowing the ground to settle and firm up under the weight of the water.
Choosing your spot: avoid tree stumps and areas close to big trees and their roots. These are some of the things to avoid, but not the only ones. Additional charges may apply if we run into tree stumps or roots. If you're unsure about a spot, ask us.
Trip charge: if we arrive and can't complete your job because something on this list wasn't done, a $250 trip charge will apply. See our Terms of Service.

Sinking your above ground pool

How deep

If you'd like to sink your pool, we don't recommend going any deeper than 2′ on most makes and models.

Digging the hole

You must dig the hole yourself or hire an excavation company to dig it. Contact us and we can give you references for excavation companies.

How big

As a rule of thumb, the hole must extend 2′ past the pool wall all the way around. For example, a 24′ round pool needs a 28′ diameter hole.

Backfilling

Brightside Pools does not backfill the hole once the pool is installed.

Disclaimer

Sinking an above ground pool may shorten the life of the pool due to ground pressure and ground water.

On install day

  1. We lift the sod. We cut it with a sod cutter and stack it wherever you'd like in the yard, so you can reuse it or easily get rid of it.
  2. We level the ground. Then we spread the masonry sand base.
  3. We level and set the upright/buttress blocks. We provide the blocks.
  4. We build the pool and install a wrinkle-free liner.
  5. We start filling with your hose. You'll have at least 4″ to 8″ of water in the pool before we leave.

Filling your pool

After we leave, you finish filling with your hose. Filling slowly with a hose costs less and is better for the liner. We only suggest having water trucked in If you're on a well, you're responsible for setting up water delivery for your installation date. We suggest Al Simons Trucking.

Electrical and Gas are your responsibility.

After we install your pool, you're responsible for having electrical and Gas run to your pool equipment. Because weather can change our install day, it's best not to schedule your electrician or Gas installer until our work is complete.

Replacing an existing pool

Putting a new pool where an old one stood.

Existing pools are tougher to install than a brand new installation. Here's what's different.

Clear the landscaping

All landscaping, rocks, mulch, and plants must be removed at least 2′ around the outside of the pool. If landscaping isn't cleared, you will be charged.

Get new sand

You must get new sand for your new pool. The old sand gets torn up and has too much debris in it to make a smooth, flat floor for your liner.

Existing decks

Many existing pools have decks. There is an upcharge to install the pool up to the deck: rounds starting at $500 and ovals starting at $800. We make every effort to set your new pool as close to your existing deck as possible. Because older and newer pool models don't always have the same size or number of top rails, a new pool may not line up exactly with your deck.

Old plumbing and parts

We won't use existing plumbing that runs under the pool, such as main drains. We also won't install old skimmers or return jets.

Your old filter system

You're welcome to reuse your old filter system, but Brightside Pools is not responsible for leaks due to age or wear and tear.

Tearing down your old pool

We can tear down and haul away your existing pool. This starts at $300 for a round pool and $500 for an oval pool. You can save money by tearing down the old pool yourself.

Liners

A new liner, set right.

Most liners last years, then fade, crack, or leak. We prep the floor and install a new liner that sits tight to the wall.

Before we arrive, your pool must be completely drained. See how to get ready

  • Overlap, beaded, and expandable liners
  • Floor and cove inspection before install
  • Filled and smoothed as it settles

Getting ready for your new liner

Drain your pool

Pump your pool all the way down before your installation date. Draining an above ground pool does no structural harm. If your pool is buried, only drain it down to the level of the ground outside the pool.

Buy new gaskets with your liner

Get new gaskets for your skimmer and return. If you have main drains, get new gaskets for those too.

Check your skimmer + return

Look at the plastic on the skimmer housing and faceplate. If it's brittle or cracked, it will have to be replaced.

Coping strips and hardware

These may need to be replaced too. We carry both. You'll see pricing when you book a liner replacement.

Washed-out floor

If your pool floor has a lot of washout, let us know ahead of time. We'll bring bags of play sand to fill in the washed-out areas. You'll see pricing when you book a liner replacement.

Your old liner

Brightside Pools does not take your old liner for disposal. We cut the old liner out of the pool and stack it neatly in a spot of your choice or place it in your trash bin.

Openings & closings

Start strong. Finish safe.

We open pools in the spring and close them at the end of the season, so your water and equipment come through a Michigan winter in good shape.

  • Opening: cover removal, equipment reconnect, startup
  • Closing: lower water, blow out lines, winterize, cover
  • Plugs, returns, and skimmer checked every visit

Spring openings

Get on the list early

Spring is our busiest time of the year, with all the new installs and liners going in. It's best to get on our pool opening list as soon as possible.

When we open pools

Most openings are done early in the season and on days that are too wet or rainy to install pools and liners. Please be flexible with us.

What an opening includes

We take off your pool cover, clean the cover, set up and test your filter system, and add opening chemicals.

Pool ladders

Brightside Pools does not touch pool ladders.

Pricing

Pool openings start at $300.

Fall closings

A slower season

Fall is our slower season, so closings are easier to schedule.

What a closing includes

We add closing chemicals, clean your filter system, and put on your cover. You must provide the pool cover.

Before your closing date

Drain your pool roughly 2″ to 4″ below the skimmer and return before your closing date.

Pricing

Pool closings start at $300. If we need to pump your pool down, you will be charged.

About grade charges.

Your pool has to sit perfectly level. Most yards slope a little, so we measure how far the ground is out of level, or "out of grade," across the spot where your pool will go.

0″–4″IncludedUp to 4 inches out of grade is part of your install at no extra cost.
Over 4″Charged per inchEvery inch beyond the first 4: $75 per inch for , $100 per inch for .

Example

A yard measures 7″ out of grade. The first 4″ are included, so 3″ are charged: 3 × $75 = $225 for a smaller pool, or 3 × $100 = $300 for a larger pool.

We measure the grade on site and go over any charge with you before we dig.

Before install day

Getting your pool permit.

Your city will want to see what you're putting in and where it's going. Here's what to bring.

1

Pool pamphlets

Bring the product pamphlets for the pool you're getting. They should show the pool style and the pump and filter system.

2

A sketch of your backyard

A simple drawing works. Draw the pool where it will go and mark how far it is from your property lines and from any structures, like your house, garage, shed, or deck.

3

Setbacks and easements

Ask your city how far the pool has to be from your property lines, your house, and other structures. Every city sets its own setbacks. Also make sure you don't have any easements in your yard where the pool will go.

Overhead lines: your pool must be at least 10′ away from any overhead lines.

FAQ

Questions, answered.

Everything customers usually ask us about booking, installs, and liners.

Booking and deposits

How does booking work?

We don't book calendar dates. We keep one job list, in the exact order deposits come in. When your turn gets close and the weather cooperates, we call you to set your day.

Why don't you give exact dates?

Installs and liner jobs depend on dry ground and good weather. Instead of promising a date we can't keep, we work the list in order and call ahead. We only book two weeks in advance, which keeps us flexible to move jobs around due to weather.

What happens to my deposit?

Your $250 deposit gets you on our job list and comes off your job total. The deposit is non-refundable.

Do openings and closings need a deposit?

No. Openings and closings don't need a deposit. Openings and closings start at $300.

How do I see pricing?

Fill out the booking form. After you choose your pool, deck, and add-ons, the Estimate tab adds everything up for you.

Service area

Do you come to my area?

We serve all of Macomb County, plus Oakland, St. Clair, Lapeer, and Wayne counties. Jobs outside Macomb County have an added charge starting at $150.

Pool installation

What sizes do you install?

Round pools from 15′ to 33′, and oval pools from 12′×17′ to 18′×40′.

Is there a trip charge?

Yes. If we arrive and can't complete your job because of customer negligence, such as sand not delivered or a pool not drained, a $250 trip charge will apply. See our Terms of Service.

Do I need to be home on installation day?

It isn't required, though we do recommend it. Someone does need to be home when the job is complete to pay the balance by cash or check.

How long does an install take?

Most installs take 4 to 8 hours, depending on pool size and how level your yard is.

What do I need to do before install day?

Get a permit from your city, call MISS DIG (811), have clean washed masonry sand delivered, get two 2′×2′ patio blocks for the filter, and mark your pool and filter spots. See the full install day checklist.

What do I need for a permit?

Your city will usually want pamphlets for your pool and its pump and filter, plus a sketch of your yard showing distances to property lines and structures. See getting your pool permit.

I have an existing pool. Do I need a permit?

No. If you're replacing an existing pool, you don't need to apply for a new permit.

Where can't my pool go?

Avoid tree stumps and areas close to big trees and their roots. Your pool must be at least 10′ from any overhead lines. Check your city's setbacks and make sure there are no easements where the pool will go. Additional charges may apply if we run into tree stumps or roots.

What are grade charges?

Grade is how far your yard is out of level where the pool will sit. Up to 4″ is included. Anything over 4″ is $75 per inch for small pools and $100 per inch for big pools.

What happens to my grass?

We cut the sod with a sod cutter and stack it wherever you'd like in the yard, so you can reuse it or easily get rid of it.

How do I fill my pool?

We start filling with your hose and leave at least 4″ to 8″ of water in the pool. You finish filling with your hose. It costs less and is better for the liner. If you're on a well, you're responsible for setting up water delivery for your installation date. We suggest Al Simons Trucking.

Who runs electrical and gas?

You do, after we install your pool. Since weather can change our install day, it's best not to schedule until our work is complete. For electrical, we recommend Nick Guthrie at (586) 713-1897. For gas, we recommend Jeff Ross at (313) 605-3167.

Can you match my pool to an existing deck?

Yes. Matching up to an existing deck is an additional charge, with rounds starting at $500 and ovals starting at $800. We make every effort to set your new pool as close to your existing deck as possible. Because older and newer pool models don't always have the same size or number of top rails, a new pool may not line up exactly with your deck.

Liner replacement

Do I need to drain my pool first?

Yes. Pump your pool all the way down before your installation date. Draining an above ground pool does no structural harm. The only exception is a buried pool, which should only be drained down to the level of the ground outside the pool.

What parts should I buy with my new liner?

New gaskets for your skimmer and return, and for your main drains if you have them. Check the plastic on your skimmer housing and faceplate. If it's brittle or cracked, it will have to be replaced.

What else might need replacing?

Coping strips and hardware may need to be replaced. We carry both. If your pool floor has a lot of washout, let us know ahead of time and we'll bring bags of play sand.

Do you take my old liner?

No. Brightside Pools does not take your old liner for disposal. We cut the old liner out of the pool and stack it neatly in a spot of your choice or place it in your trash bin.

What if my pool has a deck?

Let us know when you book. If your deck gets in the way of changing your liner, there may be an additional charge.

Terms of Service

Terms and agreements.

What you're responsible for, what we do and don't do, and how payment works. By paying a deposit or booking a job, you agree to these terms.

Last updated November 7, 2026

BookingPaymentAdditional chargesTrip chargeYour responsibilitiesWhat we do and don't doDisclaimers

1Booking and scheduling

  • A $250 deposit is required to reserve a pool installation or liner replacement. The deposit places you on our job list, comes off your job total, and is non-refundable.
  • Pool openings and closings do not require a deposit.
  • Jobs are scheduled in the order deposits are received. We do not give exact dates. Work depends on weather and ground conditions.
  • We book two weeks in advance so we can move jobs around for weather. When you book, we give you an estimated time frame, such as 2 weeks or 4 weeks.
  • Most pool openings are completed early in the season and on days that are too wet to install pools or liners. We ask that you be flexible with your scheduling.

2Payment

  • We accept cash or check only. The balance is due at the job when the work is complete.
  • You do not need to be home on the day of the job, but someone must be home when the job is complete to pay the balance.
  • Prices on our website and in your estimate are estimates. Final pricing is confirmed once we see your yard.
  • Installation prices are for pools installed on a level surface, plus or minus 4″.

3Additional charges

These are added to your total when they apply.

  • Jobs outside Macomb County: starting at $150.
  • Grade over 4″: $75 per inch for and $100 per inch for .
  • Matching up to an existing deck: rounds starting at $500, ovals starting at $800.
  • Tear down and haul away of an existing pool: rounds starting at $300, ovals starting at $500.
  • Tree stumps or roots found during the job.
  • Landscaping not cleared at least 2′ around the outside of an existing pool.
  • A deck that interferes with changing your liner.
  • Liner parts, if needed: coping strips $2 per strip; new hardware $50 for small pools and $100 for big pools; play sand $8 per bag.
  • Pumping down a pool that was not drained before a closing.

4Trip charge

If we arrive and cannot complete your job because of customer negligence, a $250 trip charge will apply. This includes, but is not limited to, any of the customer responsibilities in section 5 not being done by the job date, such as sand not delivered, the pool not drained for a liner replacement, the pool and filter spots not marked, or landscaping not cleared.

5Customer responsibilities

New pool installations

  • Obtain a permit from your city. You do not need a new permit if you are replacing an existing pool.
  • Call MISS DIG (811) to have underground utilities marked.
  • Check your city's setbacks from property lines, houses, and other structures, and make sure there are no easements where the pool will go.
  • Keep the pool at least 10′ away from any overhead lines.
  • Have clean washed masonry sand delivered (see the sand reference table). Have it delivered to the driveway as close to the backyard as possible. If it is delivered into the backyard, it must not be dumped where the pool will go.
  • Provide 2′×2′ patio blocks: two for the filter system on every new install, two more if you add a heater, and one more for a ladder pad if we install one of our decks.
  • Mark your pool spot (round: the center; oval: four corners of a rectangle) and your filter spot, 3′ off the water's edge. On an oval pool, the filter must go on one of the curved ends.
  • Choose a spot away from tree stumps and big trees or roots.
  • Have a designated spot for us to stack the sod. Disposing of the sod is your responsibility.
  • Finish filling the pool with your hose after we leave. If you are on a well, arrange water delivery for your installation date.
  • Build and install your pool ladder. We recommend waiting 4 to 5 days after installation.
  • Arrange electrical and Gas to your pool equipment after the installation is complete.

Replacing an existing pool

  • Remove all landscaping, rocks, mulch, and plants at least 2′ around the outside of the pool.
  • Provide new sand. Old sand cannot be reused.
  • Tear down the old pool yourself, unless you have booked our tear down and haul away service.

Sinking your pool

  • Dig the hole yourself or hire an excavation company. We can provide references.
  • We do not recommend going deeper than 2′ on most makes and models.
  • The hole must extend 2′ past the pool wall all the way around (for example, a 28′ diameter hole for a 24′ round pool).

Liner replacements

  • Drain the pool all the way down before the job date. A buried pool should only be drained to the level of the ground outside the pool.
  • Buy new gaskets for your skimmer, return, and any main drains.
  • Replace the skimmer housing or faceplate if the plastic is brittle or cracked.
  • Let us know ahead of time if the pool floor has a lot of washout.
  • Dispose of the old liner.

Openings and closings

  • For closings, drain the pool roughly 2″ to 4″ below the skimmer and return before the closing date.
  • For closings, provide the pool cover.

6What Brightside Pools will and will not do

We will

  • Remove the sod with a sod cutter and stack it where you choose.
  • Level the ground and spread the masonry sand base.
  • Provide, level, and set the upright and buttress blocks.
  • Build the pool and install a wrinkle-free liner.
  • Start filling the pool with your hose and leave at least 4″ to 8″ of water.
  • Cut out your old liner and stack it neatly or place it in your trash bin, then prep the floor and install your new liner.
  • Openings: remove and clean your cover, set up and test your filter system, and add opening chemicals.
  • Closings: add closing chemicals, clean your filter system, and put on your cover.
  • Tear down and haul away your existing pool, if you book this service.
  • Fit your new pool as close to your existing deck as possible.

We will not

  • Landscaping of any kind.
  • Backfilling around a sunk pool.
  • Digging holes for sunk pools.
  • Building or installing pool ladders, due to insurance liability. We also do not touch pool ladders during openings.
  • Electrical or Gas work.
  • Obtaining permits or calling MISS DIG.
  • Hauling away or disposing of sod or old liners.
  • Reusing existing plumbing under the pool, such as main drains.
  • Installing old skimmers or return jets.
  • Arranging water delivery.

7Disclaimers

  • Reused filter systems: you may reuse your old filter system, but Brightside Pools is not responsible for leaks due to age or wear and tear.
  • Sinking a pool may shorten the life of the pool due to ground pressure and ground water.
  • Existing decks: older and newer pool models don't always have the same size or number of top rails, so a new pool may not line up exactly with an existing deck.
  • Weather can change any job date.

8Licensing and insurance

Brightside Pools is a licensed and insured builder.
